column1: # Struck veins: work that has already been tried, sized, or measured and found not
# worth doing. Consult this BEFORE starting a lane -- `check_struck.py <target>`.
# Why this file exists: the `bunfig` preload change was implemented and reverted
# TWICE, costing the same 5 bun files both times, because the first retirement was
# recorded only as prose in RESUME.md -- which is now ~2300 lines and no lane reads
# end to end. A retired vein is only useful if the next lane trips over it.
#   COSTS_GREEN  implemented and measured; it loses files. Do not re-attempt as-is.
#   TOO_BIG      real and correct, but the work is out of proportion to the files.
#   BLOCKED      needs something unavailable (prebuilt JSC, docker, missing OpenSSL).
#   NOT_A_BUG    the failure is the test doing what it is supposed to do.
#   DECLINED     technically cheap, but wrong to do (gaming a metric, weakening a check).
#   LOW_YIELD    measured and it moves ~nothing; the signature over-promised.
# Columns: area <TAB> target <TAB> verdict <TAB> cost_or_size <TAB> evidence
# Append-only. If you overturn an entry, do not delete it -- add a new row whose
# evidence names the commit that overturned it, so the history stays auditable.

wave 63 audited it in full. FIVE independent divergences, not one: (1) destroy(err) never normalises a NUMBER into destroyCode + ERR_HTTP2_SESSION_ERROR the way core.js:1601-1616 does, so it emits the raw number 7; (2) closeSession must destroy every live stream WITH the session error and send GOAWAY(code) before teardown; (3) _teardown sets `closed = true`, but node's closeSession sets DESTROYED only and the test asserts `session.closed === false`; (4) no _goawayCode/_destroyCode fields exist, so `sessionCode = goawayCode || destroyCode` precedence in Http2Stream#_destroy (core.js:2437-2465) cannot be expressed and rstCode comes out 2/8 instead of 7; (5) the GOAWAY must survive a hard _teardown that destroys the socket. Fixes (3) and (4) sit on the SHARED client+server+compat stream-destroy path whose CANCEL behaviour was tuned against test-http2-client-destroy -- high regression risk for a single file. Only the low-risk piece was landed in wave 63: ERR_HTTP2_SESSION_ERROR now carries the raw numeric code (core.js:760,1611) instead of errName()

column4: net.Socket write path rewrite, whole net+http+tls surface at risk
column5: measured in wave 63: test-http-outgoing-properties, test-http-outgoing-end-cork and test-http-outgoing-message-capture-rejection all need `socket.write()` to buffer like node stream.Writable. mbun net.Socket write() pushes to _wq then `_flush()`es to the fd SYNCHRONOUSLY (js_net.cppm ~1519), so _wqLen is 0 on return: writableLength reads 0 where node reads 8 after res.write("asd"), and write() returns true where node returns false. OutgoingMessage._writeRaw/writableLength are already verbatim node -- the divergence is one layer down, in the socket. Making the flush deferred is the faithful fix but rewrites the hot write path every net/http/tls test depends on; out of proportion to 3 files for a single lane
